sections.overview: The wood sandpiper is a small migratory wader that breeds across northern Eurasia and winters mainly in Africa, southern Asia and Australasia.
sections.identification: It has spotted upperparts, yellow-green legs, a pale eyebrow and a square white rump in flight.
sections.habitat: It breeds in northern bogs and marshes; outside the breeding season it favours shallow freshwater margins, wet meadows, pools and flooded fields.
sections.diet: It takes insects and their larvae, along with worms and other small aquatic animals.
sections.behavior: It migrates between Eurasian breeding grounds and African and Asian wintering areas, often gathering in small flocks on passage.
sections.reproduction: It nests on the ground in marshes and bogs, usually laying four eggs; both parents incubate, while the male commonly tends the young after the female leaves.
sections.ecology: The spotted redshank is among its close Tringa relatives; see that profile for comparison.
sections.conservation: BirdLife Australia reports a global IUCN status of Least Concern; the RSPB lists it as Amber in the UK, a regional assessment.
